is_anopheles.evidence: The study tested Anopheles gambiae (strain RSP-H) and Anopheles funestus (strain FUMOZ-R) alongside Aedes aegypti (Page 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Refers to the Vgsc L1014S (kdr-east / L995S) mutation in the Anopheles gambiae RSP-H laboratory strain (Page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype counts, allele counts, or frequencies from a genotyped field population are reported; the paper only notes that the RSP-H laboratory colony is routinely screened to maintain 100% kdr frequency (Page 4).

african_field_population.evidence: The mosquitoes tested were strictly from permanent laboratory colonies (RSP-H, FUMOZ-R, Aedes aegypti) maintained in the Bayer CropScience insectary in Monheim, Germany (Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical laboratory bioassay study evaluating active ingredients against mosquito strains (Page 3-4).

sub_country_location.evidence: No sub-country field locations exist because only laboratory strains were tested.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: No field collection years are reported.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary data needed; study is ineligible due to laboratory colony usage.

assessment.summary: This study conducted surface contact bioassays testing transfluthrin and other pyrethroids with/without PBO against standard laboratory strains (Anopheles gambiae RSP-H, Anopheles funestus FUMOZ-R, and Aedes aegypti). It did not sample or genotype any African field populations.
exclusion_reasons: No field-collected mosquito populations from Africa were studied (only permanent laboratory colonies RSP-H and FUMOZ-R were used).
No extractable genotype data for field populations are reported.
